text:
Maya S: FYI — ACME reported a sudden p99 jump this morning, started ~04:20 UTC. They see 503s and sporadic auth retries. They say requests started timing out and backlog hit during a big inference burst.

acme-support: seeing a lot of 'instance OOM' errors and long tails. p50 unchanged, p95 ~700ms -> p95 ~1.2s, p99 -> 4.2s.

Maya S: Here's the snippet from the host where the worst latency happened:```
[2026-03-12T04:21:03Z] GPU0: alloc failed: out of memory (requested 1.6GiB)
[2026-03-12T04:21:04Z] kv_cache: slab_evict triggered, reclaimed 1.1GiB, free 0.2GiB
[2026-03-12T04:21:05Z] inference: fallback to slow-path, latency spike
```

Jordan C: Are they on Dedicated pool 'dedicated-8'? any recent model changes or config rollouts?

acme-support: yes, dedicated-8. No model change on our side; workload shifted (more long-context chat sessions).

Ravi P: likely KV growth from long-context prompts combined with slab fragmentation. Two quick asks: 1) can we get slab density and eviction counters for the node? 2) is allocator tuning (compaction) enabled?

Lin O: I'm oncall — collecting /proc/meminfo, nvidia-smi and our runtime memstats now. Also please run a debug dump from that pod:```sh
rdwctl debug memdump --node dedicated-8-12 --out /tmp/memdump.json
```

Maya S: Did a quick check of the metrics — slab_evictions spiked at 04:20, avg_free_slab dropped below 15% and per-tenant kv_size shows a hot tenant (~acme-tenant-17) using 65% of its allotted KV.

Ravi P: short-term mitigation options:
- enable transient compaction on that pool (alloc.tune.slab_compact=1)
- increase eviction aggressiveness for that tenant (kv.max_resident -> lower)
- route ACME to a warm fallback service (cpu-inference) for heavy long-context flows while we stabilize

Jordan C: CS asked for an ETA — can we do compaction without a restart and what's the risk?

Ravi P: compaction is safe but noisy; it will cause brief p50 regressions while it runs (reclaims memory). Estimate 6–12 minutes to compact the hot node. If we also increase eviction aggressiveness, that should reduce OOMs in ~5 minutes.

Lin O: started compaction toggle on dedicated-8-12 now (rollout 1/3). Monitoring metrics. Also opened emergency routing rule to spill ACME to cpu-fallback if p95>2s for 2min.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 2026-03-12-ACME-GPU-OOM created — priority P2. Assigned: Ravi P, Lin O, Maya S.

acme-support: thanks, seeing fewer OOMs already and p99 down to ~2.1s. We'll keep traffic steady for 30m.

Maya S: plan: 1) finish compaction on all nodes in pool (Ravi), 2) permanently lower kv.max_resident for acme-tenant-17 and add a soft quota (Jordan to coordinate with customer), 3) add a transient dialdown policy in network for long-context heavy routes, 4) follow-up postmortem.

Ravi P: also going to propose an allocator tuning patch: enable periodic slab defrag (config: alloc.tune.slab_defrag=periodic, interval=15m) in staging and run canary next week.

Lin O: compaction finished on node 1/3, node2 compaction in progress. p99 trending down on those nodes.

Jordan C: I'll draft a note to ACME explaining mitigation steps and ask them to limit new very-long contexts for 24h while we tune.

acme-support: appreciated. will confirm when traffic stabilizes.

Maya S: closing loop — we've got mitigations live, owners assigned, and a follow-up eval to detect KV growth patterns automatically. Will update incident once postmortem scheduled. :thumbsup:
